overview: The Community Preservation Committee approved several major fiscal year 2026 funding recommendations, including park lighting and historical restorations, and authorized a small grant for a historic site survey.

items.title: Brooks Estate Archaeological Survey
items.summary: Approved a $10,000 small grant for an archaeological sensitivity report at the Brooks Estate and neighboring cemetery parcel. The approval includes a condition that the Historical Commission coordinate with conservation restriction holders and the Brooks Estate Land Trust.

items.title: Fiscal Year 2026 Budget and Project Overview
items.summary: Reviewed the available funding for the remaining four fiscal year 2026 projects, confirming approximately $2.6 million in available reserves across various categories. The committee determined that the current budget could accommodate all remaining requests.

items.title: Angel of Victory and Peace Fountain Restoration
items.summary: Approved $167,800 for the restoration of the World War II fountain. The recommendation requires the submission of a long-term maintenance plan.

items.title: Cross Street Cemetery Restoration Phase 2
items.summary: Approved $126,500 for monument restoration and repairs to the perimeter wall. The committee increased the funding amount from a previously discussed lower tier to include the wall restoration.

items.title: Shiloh Baptist Church Window Restoration Phase 2
items.summary: Approved $150,000 for stained glass window restoration with conditions requiring schematic drawings and carpentry cost estimates before disbursement. A motion to increase the grant by $35,000 failed due to concerns regarding fiscal precedent and the scope of work.

items.title: Tufts Park Field Lighting Improvements
items.summary: Approved $432,000 for lighting at Tufts Park Field 2. Conditions were added requiring the city to preserve and reuse the lighting equipment if future park renovations necessitate its removal.

items.title: Application Process and 2026 Meeting Calendar
items.summary: Discussed strategies for improving community outreach and finalized the 2026 schedule, which includes an annual public hearing in March and a project presentation cycle in the autumn. Members suggested using QR codes in parks and community bulletin boards to solicit project ideas from residents.

subject: Fiscal Year 2026 Community Preservation Funding
